To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bundling CA with sub-surface irrigation technology is a viable strategy to design sustainable intensive cereal systems in North-West India.
bundling of CA with sub-surface drips irrigation (CA+) in rice-wheat and maize-wheat systems can save 58 and 95% irrigation water and improve profitability by 30% compared to farmer practices.
CA+ practices in RW and MW system recorded higher productivity and profitability with reduced irrigation water and N use compared with ScI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of productive, profitable and water use efficient intensive cereal-based systems by bundling CA and sub-surface drip irrigations.
the design and evaluation of productive, profitable and resource-use-efficient cereal systems through bunding of precision agronomic innovations in North-West India.
the design of profitable and sustainable RW and MW systems by bundling precision agronomy and sub-surface drip systems in the North-West region of India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bundling of precision agronomic innovations (CA+ sub-surface drip) in intensive cereal systems is a promising option for transitioning towards sustainable agriculture.
bundling CA with sub-surface drips irrigation system is a promising strategy to design profitable and sustainable intensive cereal systems in water-scarce regions of North-West India.
CA+ in RW systems is a profitable option for farmers with 80% of subsidy and CA+ in MW system is profitable option for farmers without subsidy in North-West India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bundling CA with sub-surface irrigation is a promising option for transitioning towards agricultural water, nitrogen and energy use efficiency in the North-West Indian intensive cereal cropping systems.
the bundling of CA with sub-surface irrigation is a promising technology to achieve sustainable intensification of intensive cereal systems in North-West India.

bundling of sub-surface drip with conservation agriculture practices can be an effective option for designing profitable, irrigation water, nitrogen and energy use-efficient intensive cereal systems for transitioning to sustainable agriculture in north-west India.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bundling of CA with sub-surface drips irrigation system is a viable strategy for transitioning towards sustainable agricultural systems in North-West India.
bundling of CA and sub-surface drip systems is a win-win situation for farmers, environment and society.

bundling of precision agronomic innovations (CA, sub-surface drip and precision N management) can be a viable strategy to transition from flood irrigated, high external input intensive cereal systems to water, N, energy use efficient, high external input use sparing systems.
